# Introduction and setup

This vignette aims to introduce the basic functionality of the SIMBA package and show the structure of the H5 files integral to its use. 

Here and in the manuscript, we use the data and metadata from [Zeevi et al.](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.cell.2015.11.001) as input for different case-control simulation frameworks.

```{r setup}
library(tidyverse) # for data wrangling
library(simbaR)    #
data(toy_example)  # example data
```


# 1. Simulate metagenomic data

We begin with setting up some minimal parameters for our simulations. Since we begin with a raw count table, we provide some filtering parameters including prevalence and abundance cutoffs, and a pseudocount value. These will be stored in the .h5 file when the simulation is created. 

`subset_size`, `ab.scale`, and `prev.scale` can be vectors of multiple values, and `prev_scale` is a unique requirement of our signal implantation framework (secondary effect size introducing prevalence shifts between groups in addition to abundance shifts, present in all frameworks).


## Signal implantation framework (without confounders)

Next, we will do the same simulation and subset generation with our implantation framework. 

Expected time on a standard laptop: about 12 seconds.

```{r signal.implantation.sim}
#Parameters
# filtering parameters
ab.cutoff <- 1e-04 #eliminates features that have less than this abundance (presumably across all samples)
prev.cutoff <- 0.05 #eliminates features with less than this prevalence
log.n0 <- 1e-05

# other parameters for the simulations
prop.markers <- 0.1
class.balance <- 0.5
subset_size <- c(100,350)

# effect sizes
ab.scale <- c(1.0, 2.0)
prev.scale <- 0.2
```

Signal implantation

```{r signal.implantation.sim}

# give the simulation a filename
sim.implant <- 'implantation_example.h5'

# create simulations
system.time(
  create.data.simulation(feat = toy.feat,
                meta = toy.meta,
                sim.location = sim.implant,
                sim.type ='cross-section',
                sim.method ='resampling',
                filt.params = list(ab.cutoff=as.numeric(ab.cutoff),
                                   prev.cutoff=prev.cutoff,
                                   log.n0=as.numeric(log.n0)),
                sim.params = list(ab.scale=ab.scale,
                                  prev.scale=prev.scale,
                                  prop.markers=prop.markers,
                                  conf=NULL,
                                  class.balance=class.balance,
                                  feature.type='all',
                                  repeats=10)))

# create testing indices
system.time(
  create.test.idx(sim.location=sim.implant,
                subsets=subset_size,
                repetitions=10))
```

# Reading Files

```{r}
temp <- h5ls(sim.implant,recursive=FALSE)

subset350=idx.all[['subset_350']]
```

# 3. Apply LIMMA differential abundance test

To run a differential abundance test, SIMBA uses its `apply.test` function, which works on one H5 group (effect size combination) at a time.

```{r,warning=FALSE}
temp = h5ls(sim.implant,recursive=FALSE)
groups = setdiff(temp$name, c('original_data', 'simulation_parameters'))

system.time(
  pvals_test <- groups %>%
    map(~ apply.test(
      # full simulation file
      sim.location = sim.implant, 
      # which effect size combination
      group = ., 
      # which subset size(s)
      subset = c(100,350),
      # which normalization method (pass = none)
      norm = 'pass', 
      # differential abundance test
      test = 'limma')) %>%
    flatten()
)

```

Applying LIMMA Directly

```{r}
temp = h5ls(sim.implant,recursive=FALSE)
groups = setdiff(temp$name, c('original_data', 'simulation_parameters'))

#Applying Limma to each group 
pvals_groups=list()

for(group in groups){
  
  #extracting test data matrix from group
  complete_group = h5read(sim.implant, group)
  params <- h5read(file = sim.implant, name = "simulation_parameters")
  
  #Features matrix to analyse
  features = complete_group$features
  colnames(features) <- complete_group$sample_names
  rownames(features) <- complete_group$feature_names
  
  #Initialising list of pvalue matrices for each subset
  pvals_subsets = list()
  
  #Iterating through subsets
  subsets = names(complete_group$test_idx)
  for (subset in subsets) {
    
    #Getting Subset repeat indices
    subset_idx = complete_group[['test_idx']][[subset]]
    
    #Labelling each row for each repeat
    rownames(subset_idx) <- params$test_idx$names #labelling each repeat for each subset. 
    
    #Extracting group labels for subset repeats
    label=subset_idx["label",]
    
    #Subset repeat indices
    subset_repeats = subset_idx[which(grepl("^rep[0-9]*$", rownames(subset_idx))), 
                            , drop = FALSE]
    
    conf.mat=NULL #no confounders at this stage
    
    #Initialising p-value matrix 
    pvals=data.frame(row.names = complete_group$feature_names)
  
    #Iterating through repeats
    for(i in 1:dim(subset_repeats)[1]){
      
      #Dataset to be tested
      df.test = features[,subset_repeats[i,]] #taking ith repeat of subset
      
      #Normalising Data
      df.test = simbaR:::norm.data(df.test, norm="pass", log.n0) #normalisation step,  currently no normalisation
      
      #Applying limma
      fit = limma::lmFit(df.test,design=data.frame(intercept = -1, label))
      res = limma::eBayes(fit)
      
      #Extracting pvalue matrix
      colname = paste0("rep_",i)
      pvals[[colname]] = res$p.value[,"label"]
      
    }
    pvals_subsets[[subset]] <- as.matrix(pvals)
  }
  pvals_groups[[group]] <- pvals_subsets
}

```
# 4. Evaluate test results

To evaluate differential abundance test results, the p-value matrix above can be fed to the `eval.test` SIMBA function, which uses the ground truth stored in marker_idx for each group to tabulate a confusion matrix, precision, recall, AUROC, and a FDR for each element.

```{r}
test_group = 'ab1_prev1_rep1' 
eval.test(
      # full simulation file
      sim.location = sim.implant,
      # which effect size combination
      group = test_group,
      # single p-value matrix
      res.mat = pvals_test[[test_group]]$subset_350,
      # desired significance threshold
      alpha = 0.05)


```
```{r}
test_group = 'ab1_prev1_rep1' 
eval.test(
      # full simulation file
      sim.location = sim.implant,
      # which effect size combination
      group = test_group,
      # single p-value matrix
      res.mat = pvals_groups[[test_group]]$subset_350,
      # desired significance threshold
      alpha = 0.05)
```



```{r}
test_group = 'ab1_prev1_rep1'

eval.test(
      # full simulation file
      sim.location = sim.implant,
      # which effect size combination
      group = test_group,
      # single p-value matrix
      res.mat = pvals_groups[[test_group]][['subset_350']],
      # desired significance threshold
      alpha = 0.05)
```
